html:
The Yamhill, or Yamel, were a band of the Kalapuya people of the Willamette Valley in Oregon, living along the Yamhill River west of today's Portland. They spoke a Northern Kalapuya language.

The Kalapuya burned the valley grasslands every year to keep them open for camas, acorns and deer. A malaria epidemic in the early 1830s killed most of the valley's people. Then settlers arriving on the Oregon Trail from the 1840s took the land. In 1855 the Kalapuya signed the Willamette Valley Treaty, and in 1856 they were moved to the Grand Ronde reservation, where their descendants are part of the Confederated Tribes of Grand Ronde. Neighbouring bands included the Mohawk Kalapuya to the south.
